elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 13 retains automatic renewal ("This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods") and no mutual-written-agreement renewal is substituted, so this element depends on all conditional automatic-renewal elements being satisfied; the 60-day reminder and CPI/3% cap elements are not satisfied, so the gateway fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 13: "renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods" — each renewal term is 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 13: "unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year" — Client's opt-out requires only 30 days' notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Renewal is automatic, so the condition applies, but neither Section 13 nor the inserted sentence imposes any obligation on TrueLink to notify or remind Client in advance of a renewal. Operative language would need an express TrueLink reminder obligation at least 60 days before each renewal date.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence caps increases at a flat five percent ("TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term"), not the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 13 requires "written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year" — a 30-day window, within the 60-day ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" scanned only the inserted operation text; the requirement is satisfied by existing operative language, so no edit is needed.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term." This closes the gap left by Section 6, which freezes Hosting Services costs only "for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement".

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the retained 30-day non-renewal window already sits inside the 60-day ceiling, and the single inserted sentence supplies the 5% renewal uplift cap that Section 6's one-year freeze left open.

Preferred level fails on two elements: no TrueLink reminder obligation 60 days before renewal, and the cap is a flat 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%. Both are correctly not pressed and are noted in the comment rather than mis-claimed.

Minimality holds: one added sentence, no deletions, no survival tail, procedure, expense or damages boilerplate, and the cap is set exactly at the 5% fallback threshold rather than above or below it. Extending the cap to "TrueLink's fees" rather than only Hosting Services fees is a customer-favourable scoping choice within the same checklist element, not an added requirement outside it.

Intent preserved: the Section 6 first-year freeze and most-favoured-rate covenant, the Section 12 termination cross-reference, the Section 2/3 early-termination provisos and the 30/60-day name-server and hosting-migration timelines all survive unchanged, and confining the cap to "any renewal term" avoids any contradiction with the first-year freeze. No undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in substance): the inserted sentence is appended after Section 13 without its own numbering; consider placing it in Section 6 alongside the existing pricing covenants or labelling it as a new sentence of Section 6 so the pricing mechanics stay together.
